references.text: Refers to the value and significance of wisdom, which can be compared to seeking and valuing the precious pearl in Matthew 13:46.
Encourages seeking what is truly valuable without cost, paralleling how the man in Matthew 13:46 sold all he had to buy the pearl.
Moses considered Christ's disgrace greater riches than Egypt's treasures, which resembles the action of the man in Matthew 13:46 who sold everything to buy the pearl.
Refers to Christ as a living stone, rejected by people but chosen and precious to God, which can be seen in light of the value of the pearl in Matthew 13:46.
